q: Put the events that lead to ovulation in order, earliest first.
key: Each step creates the signal for the next: FSH grows follicles, their estradiol flips pituitary feedback, and the LH surge completes meiosis I and ruptures the follicle.
items: FSH recruits a cohort of antral follicles
Early follicular FSH rescues a group of follicles from atresia, which is why FSH is highest at the start of the cycle.
One dominant follicle emerges and makes more estradiol
The follicle with the most FSH receptors keeps growing as FSH falls, while its estradiol and inhibin starve the others.
Estradiol stays high for about two days
Sustained high estradiol is the trigger that flips the pituitary from negative to positive feedback.
The pituitary releases the LH surge
Positive feedback produces a surge of LH that begins about a day and a half before ovulation.
The LH surge restarts meiosis, so the oocyte finishes meiosis I and arrests again in metaphase II.
The follicle ruptures and releases the oocyte
Proteases activated by the surge weaken the follicle wall, and ovulation follows about 36 hours after the surge begins.
